transcript.text: From what you have described, the most likely cause is the drive belt. On a corded upright the brush is driven by a rubber belt under the base plate (unplug it first; the plate usually unclips or has a few screws). Is the belt snapped, stretched or off its pulley, or is it in place and tight?

I can't turn it over, my back. It's the red Henry and nothing happens at all when I switch it on. There's some old tape on the cable near the plug, and it came on once for a second when I moved the wire.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is a damaged mains cable or plug. Try the socket with something else, and check the switch on the vacuum. If the plug has a fuse (UK plugs do), a 13A fuse can be swapped — unplugged. Look along the cable for cuts or damage too. Was it the socket, switch or fuse (and is it sorted), is the cable or plug damaged, or is the supply fine?
The lamp works in the socket so that's fine. The switch clicks ok I think. I haven't got a screwdriver or a spare fuse so can't do the plug. The tape on the cable near the plug is a bit bent.
From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
